name: pixel-world
//: Read the comment in .devcontainer/Dockerfile first. Containment here is a function of what is NOT mounted and NOT installed, and every mount below is a hole in that boundary — adding one is a security decision, not a convenience one. Before adding a mount, ask: does this need to be writable, does it carry a credential, and is there a path that does not require it? For the history: this list started deliberately short, but agent use of this repo has grown since, and the mounting style has converged on the bot-owned lab projects in ~/lab — msmtp so an unsupervised run can send its summary, the read-only instruction and spend files, the wiki, and the lab-bot Pi auth file for model calls. What it still does not inherit from them is the lab-bot git PAT (git here uses the repo-scoped PAT), the host tool directory, or the docker socket; the only file it can write outside the container remains a push to this repository.
//mounts-why: Six mounts, all read-only, and each is deliberate. (1) the repo-scoped GitHub PAT, at the same relative path it has on the host so git-askpass.sh needs no container-specific variant — NOT the ~/.config/jef directory, which would also expose the jefscad PAT once it exists. (2) ~/.msmtprc, so an unsupervised run can send its summary email. (3) spend.py, read-only because an agent that can edit its own cap check has no cap. (4) ~/tools/llm-instructions, the generic working instructions for pair, tdd and unsupervised mode, read-only for the same class of reason: the rules a session operates under must not be editable by that session. (5) the wiki: the agent reads the distilled kb fundamentals, this project's implementation pages, and other projects' pages when a decision has cross-project implications — but cannot write, because the wiki is the one tier where an undetected error compounds instead of being caught. Proposals go to notes/wiki-proposals/ and a human promotes them (see wiki-sync.md). (6) the lab-bot agent's Pi auth file, ~/.config/lab-bot/pi-auth.json, which is the OpenRouter key — agent-scoped rather than repo-scoped: it is the bot's own credential, shared with the other sessions that use it, not one cut for this repo. NOT ~/.ssh (the personal key reaches every repo on the account, including the wiki), NOT the rest of ~/.config/lab-bot (only that one file is mounted), NOT ~/.aws or ~/.azure, NOT the host tool directory, NOT the docker socket (this repo builds nothing locally — its images, if any, are not its business).

remoteEnv.//git: GIT_ASKPASS points at the tracked script that reads the mounted PAT. GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 stops a failed lookup from falling back to an interactive prompt, which in an unattended run hangs until the run is killed. GIT_SSH_COMMAND=/bin/false is a second line of defence behind the missing ssh binary: even if one is added later, git cannot silently fall back to SSH.
